id: -1447-進攻米坦尼（第八次敘利亞戰役）
theater: 幼發拉底河畔至米坦尼邊境

battle.name: 進攻米坦尼（第八次敘利亞戰役）
battle.theater: 幼發拉底河畔至米坦尼邊境
battle.brief: 前1447年，圖特摩斯三世再度自南敘利亞出發，這次目標越過幼發拉底河直指米坦尼本土：大軍在卡爾凱美什一帶強渡，擊潰大王麾下的胡里聯軍，逼得米坦尼遣使求和。埃及步兵以長矛列成前排，弓手覆蓋兩翼，車兵趁敵陣裂開時投入，圍城則以長矛與攻城塔壓住城頭，是第八次敘利亞戰役的北界推進。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 交戰的兩方是埃及新王國第十八王朝與以胡里人為核心的米坦尼聯盟。埃及方面由法老圖特摩斯三世親任全軍最高統帥，國王自領近衛與王牌弓手隊出戰，軍隊骨架是步兵：中央是持圓盾、長柄銅斧與長矛的重裝步兵，兩翼與前鋒由數量最多的埃及弓手展開，另有數百輛雙輪戰車留作突擊與追擊；傭兵與徵召兵中包括來自黎凡特、努比亞與西部沙漠的謝爾登人、麥傑人與沙漠部族，軍中文書記錄口糧配給與徵發物資。米坦尼方面是上美索不達米亞的胡里王國，國王自稱「大王」，都城瓦舒卡尼在今日土耳其與敘利亞邊境一帶，位置至今仍未確定；大王以宗主身分控制敘利亞諸邦——卡脫納、圖尼普、阿勒頗、比布魯斯與西頓——並在幼發拉底河中游的卡爾凱美什與埃馬爾扶植親信，聯軍以步兵、車兵與胡里弓手為骨幹，並得到巴比倫的默契支持：彼時巴比倫王布爾納布里什一世雖在形式上與埃及平行通書，往上美索不達米亞方向輸送的銅、錫與青金石，實際上多經米坦尼一線轉運。赫梯此時仍據安納托利亞高原，尚未南下爭奪敘利亞，與本戰役只有間接關係。
countriesEn: The two belligerents were Egypt of the Eighteenth Dynasty and the Mitanni coalition built around Hurrian power. On the Egyptian side the supreme commander was the pharaoh Thutmose III, who led the host in person, taking the royal guard and the elite corps of bowmen with him; the framework of the army was infantry: heavy foot with round shields, long-handled bronze axes and long spears in the centre, Egyptian archers — the largest contingent — on the wings and in the vanguard, and several hundred two-wheeled chariots held back for breakthrough and pursuit; mercenaries and conscripts included Sherden, Medjay and desert tribes from the Levant, Nubia and the western oases, while army scribes kept ration tallies and requisition lists. On the Mitanni side stood the Hurrian kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia, whose king called himself the Great King and whose capital, Washukanni, lay somewhere on the border between modern Turkey and Syria and has never been located with certainty; the Great King held the Syrian city-states — Qatna, Tunip, Aleppo, Byblos and Sidon — as his own subordinates, and at Carchemish and Emar on the middle Euphrates he had installed clients of his own, while the coalition fought with infantry, chariot troops and Hurrian archers, with the tacit support of Babylonia: although Burnaburiash I of Babylon corresponded with Egypt as an equal, the copper, tin and lapis lazuli moving down from Upper Mesopotamia travelled largely along the Mitanni line. The Hittites at this date still held the Anatolian plateau and had not yet come south to contest Syria, so their part in this war is indirect.
people: 核心人物是埃及法老圖特摩斯三世（Menkheperre），在位約三十八年（約前1479年至前1425年），這場戰役是他統治中期的又一次大規模北征。國王本人統率全軍，並非坐鎮後方；日常指揮由宰相與「弓箭手隊長」一類的軍職分擔，軍中文書留下逐日行程與地名清單，後人才能循名單還原路線。對面的米坦尼之主是自稱「大王」的胡里君主，具體人名在文獻中排序不一，一般認為屬圖特基什一系；前1400年代在阿瑪納字母中與埃及通信、屢次索取銀兩的圖胥拉塔，則是這位大王的後繼者。敘利亞方面，阿勒頗一系的王公與卡脫納、圖尼普的統治者是各自與大王結盟的城邦領袖，阿勒頗之王的名號在埃及文獻中拼法不一，甚至是不是同一人都有爭議。巴比倫王布爾納布里什一世亦在通信中與埃及平行通書，態度更接近仲裁者而非交戰方。戰後的外交主角轉到米坦尼：圖胥拉塔在阿門霍特普三世治下致書埃及乞求黃金與雕像，甚至把自己的女兒送進埃及宮中，把戰場上的失敗轉成曠日持久的請願，而埃及那邊，圖特摩斯三世本人也很快離開人間，這段勝利的受益者其實是他身後的王朝。
peopleEn: The central figure is the Egyptian pharaoh Thutmose III (Menkheperre). He reigned for about thirty-eight years, roughly from 1479 to 1425 BC, and this war was another large northern campaign of the middle part of his reign. The king commanded the host in person rather than directing it from the rear, with day-to-day control delegated to the vizier and to offices such as the chief of the bowmen, while army scribes drew up day-by-day itineraries and place-name lists, which is how the route can be reconstructed at all today. The opposing ruler of Mitanni was the Hurrian monarch who styled himself the Great King; his personal name is ordered differently in different documents, and he is generally placed in the line of Tutkigsh, while Tushratta — the king who corresponded with Egypt in the Amarna letters of the fifteenth century and asked for silver again and again — was his successor. On the Syrian side, the dynast of the Aleppo line and the rulers of Qatna and Tunip were city-state leaders, each of them allied with the Great King; even the name of the king of Aleppo varies in Egyptian sources, and whether the references point to one man or more than one is disputed. Burnaburiash I of Babylon also corresponded with Egypt on equal terms, and his position was closer to that of an arbiter than of a belligerent. The diplomatic protagonist of the aftermath shifts to Mitanni: Tushratta wrote to Egypt under Amenhotep III asking for gold and for a statue, and even sent his own daughter into the Egyptian court, converting a defeat on the field into a long petition — and on the Egyptian side Thutmose III himself died soon afterwards, so the beneficiary of that victory was in fact the dynasty behind him.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及長矛：早王朝時期已出現的制式長矛，銅或青銅矛頭（柳葉形、有中脊、有套筒）綁在木杆上，杆身以皮條或麻繩纏紮加固，矛尖既能刺穿軟甲與皮甲，也能在衝撞中承受反作用力。到第十八王朝時，這種長矛已不再是主角，卻遠未退場：它是重裝步兵前排最廉價、最普遍的近戰兵器，也是埃及邊防堡壘與城垣守備的標準武備，因為守城需要的不是砍劈，而是把來犯者擋在台階之下。本卡兵器在這場戰役裡的位置正是在這兩處：遠征途中的正面會戰，長矛列成的密集矛牆在弓手箭雨之後迎住聯軍步兵與車兵；渡河之後的圍城，埃及人把長矛架在斜坡與雲梯旁，對準城頭與爬梯的人。埃及步兵整體裝備還包括角、筋、木製的複合弓，弓手是軍隊中數量最多的一環，箭簇以燙硬打製；近戰兵另有月牙形青銅短劍、長柄銅斧與短匕。車兵是突破與追擊的力量：木輪雙輪車，四匹馬挽的車漸多，御者與射手同車。攻城方面備有攻城塔、撞錘與填土斜坡，弓手與標槍先壓制城頭。遠程火力仍以弓為主，胡里與敘利亞弓手同用複合弓，聯軍近戰則以銅斧與雙刃斧為主。補給靠驢騾隊與牛車運糧，以及城邦徵發的穀物、葡萄酒與金屬；銅來自西奈與亞洲，錫與青金石經巴比倫方向運來。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian spear: a standard long spear that already existed in the Early Dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head — leaf-shaped, with a midrib and a socket — bound to a wooden shaft, the shaft reinforced by thongs or cord wrappings, so that the point could both pierce soft and leather armour and survive the recoil of a charge. By the Eighteenth Dynasty the spear was no longer the star of the show, but it was very far from retired: it was the cheapest and most universal close-combat arm of the heavy infantry in the front rank, and the standard arm of the Egyptian frontier fortresses and city walls, because what a siege needs is not chopping but the means of holding attackers below the steps. That is precisely the two places where this card's weapon belongs in this war: in the pitched battle on the march, the close-packed spear wall met the coalition infantry and chariots after the archers' arrow-fall; and in the siege that followed the crossing, the Egyptians planted their spears along the ramp and beside the ladders, pointed at the wall and at the men coming up them. The rest of the Egyptian infantry loadout included composite bows of horn, sinew and wood, and the archers were the largest single contingent in the army, their arrowheads hardened in fire; the close-combat foot also carried the inward-curving bronze khopesh, long-handled bronze axes and short daggers. Chariotry was the force for breakthrough and pursuit: two-wheeled cars of wood, with four-horse teams becoming commoner, the driver and the archer riding together. For siege work the Egyptians had towers, battering rams and earth ramps, and they cleared the wall with arrows and javelins before the assault. Meanwhile the principal long-range weapon on both sides remained the bow: Hurrian and Syrian archers used composite bows as well, and the coalition's close combat turned on bronze axes and double-bit axes. Supply came up with donkey and mule trains and ox carts carrying grain, together with the requisitioned grain, wine and metal of the city-states; the copper came from Sinai and from Asia, while tin and lapis lazuli arrived by way of Babylon.
tactics: 埃及的遠征有一套固定做法：軍隊不整隊行軍，而分成數路縱隊推進——中央縱隊沿大道走，左翼沿奧龍特斯河谷作先鋒，右翼貼近海岸與山麓作掩護，三路在會合處同時壓上；沿途每日宿營前派出偵察，軍中文書把道路、村落與渡口記在行程表上，後人甚至能從殘存的地名表裡還原行軍路線。渡過幼發拉底河是全戰最要緊的一步：河上沒有橋，須以船、筏或浮橋分批渡過，埃及人甚至先造好船、把船由海路運到陸路再搬過陸地，以便從北岸登船；春末夏初正是安納托利亞融雪之際，河面最寬、水流最急，守方只要把渡口封住，遠征即告中止。渡河之後大軍立刻圍城或設營，把城內的水井與耕地控制在自己手裡。會戰陣形以步兵正面與弓手在兩翼展開，戰車不放在前線，而是留待敵陣出現缺口時一齊投入，衝開之後才讓步兵帶著長矛與月牙劍湧入缺口作近身格鬥；長矛手在前列相互搭著肩背，把前列變成一堵推不倒的牆，而矛的長度正好頂住失去衝力的散兵。攻城多以圍而不打與突擊並用：先用弓手與標槍清理城頭，再以雲梯攀城或斷糧迫降，必要時堆土築斜坡，把車兵送上城牆高度。外交與戰爭並行：對敘利亞城邦用「宗主—納貢」收編，對「大王」則以軍威迫其送來黃金與青金石，甚至索取條約副本與結盟印璽，把戰場上的結果直接換算成外交上的收益。
tacticsEn: The Egyptians had a settled method for a distant campaign. The army did not march as one column: it advanced in several parallel columns, the central one on the main road, the left wing through the valley of the Orontes as the vanguard, the right wing close to the coast and the foothills as cover, the three closing together at a point of rendezvous. Scouting parties went out before each night's halt, and army scribes entered roads, villages and fords in the itinerary, so that the line of march can be reconstructed from a surviving topographical list of place names. The crossing of the Euphrates was the most critical step of the whole war: there were no bridges, the host had to be ferried across in boats, rafts or pontoons, and the Egyptians even had ships built and then carried overland by portage so that they could board from the northern bank; in the last month of spring and the first of summer the Anatolian snowmelt was at its height, the river at its widest and swiftest, and if the fords were held the expedition was over. Once across, the army at once invested the city or entrenched, taking control of the wells and the fields inside it. In pitched battle the line was infantry frontally with archers on the wings; the chariots were not committed to the front but were held back and launched together when a gap opened in the enemy formation, and only then did the infantry with their spears and their khopesh pour through the gap and finish the business at close quarters. The spearmen in the leading files overlapped their shields and shoulders so that the front became a wall that could not easily be pushed aside, and the reach of their spears was exactly the reach needed against troops whose momentum had been broken. Sieges combined blockade with sudden assault: the wall was first cleared with arrows and javelins, then scaled with ladders or reduced by starvation, and where necessary earth was tipped up into a ramp to bring the chariots to the height of the rampart. Diplomacy ran alongside the war: the Syrian city-states were folded into a system of overlordship and tribute, while the Great King was pressed by force of arms to send gold and lapis lazuli, and even to hand over a copy of a treaty and a seal of alliance, so that what was won on the field was converted directly into diplomatic gain.
data: 可核對的數字如下。年代通常記作前1447年，跨入前1446年，屬圖特摩斯三世在位中期的一次北征；圖特摩斯三世在位約三十八年，約前1479年至前1425年。距離方面，由底比斯到幼發拉底河畔的卡爾凱美什直線約一千一百公里，沿軍用道迂迴後超過一千五百公里；由尼羅河三角洲東界到卡爾凱美什約一千公里；以每日二十五至三十公里的行軍速度計算，全程需五十日上下，遠征往返的時間遠超此數。河寬方面，幼發拉底河在卡爾凱美什一帶寬約一百至一百五十公尺，春季融雪期水勢最盛。兵力方面，埃及方面的核心步兵一般估計在數千至一萬之間，弓手占其中多數，戰車常在數百輛的量級，部分估算高至逾千輛；對面聯軍靠各城邦拼湊，總數亦在數千至一萬上下，車兵比例低於埃及。物資來源同樣可查：埃及從西奈的塞伊納等銅礦取銅，從巴比倫方向取得青金石，銅與青金石多經米坦尼一線轉運，這說明商路正是爭端所在；另從黎巴嫩海岸運雪松木入埃及，在新王國盛期達到高峰。戰果數字須打折扣：埃及碑文以擄獲人數、馬匹與金銀器計功，數量常被後世學者調低數倍，宜視為宣傳量度而非統計。最硬的證據是阿瑪納字母：現存約三百五十封，其中逾二百封涉及米坦尼。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The date is normally given as 1447 BC, running into 1446 BC, and the war belongs to one of the northern campaigns of the middle of Thutmose III's reign; he reigned about thirty-eight years, roughly from 1479 to 1425 BC. As for distances: the straight line from Thebes to Carchemish on the Euphrates is about eleven hundred kilometres, rather more than fifteen hundred by the military road once the route detours; from the eastern edge of the Nile Delta to Carchemish is about a thousand kilometres; at a marching rate of twenty-five to thirty kilometres a day the whole thing took something like fifty days, and the round trip took far longer. The Euphrates at Carchemish is about one hundred to one hundred and fifty metres wide, and in the spring flood it is at its strongest. On numbers of men: the Egyptian core infantry is generally estimated at several thousand up to ten thousand, with archers forming the majority of it, and chariots usually counted in the hundreds, though some estimates run past a thousand; the opposing coalition was assembled from the several city-states and came to a comparable several thousand up to ten thousand, with a lower proportion of chariot troops. The flow of supplies can be traced just as well: Egypt drew copper from the mines of Sinai such as Timna, and lapis lazuli from the Babylonian direction, and both moved largely through the Mitanni line, which shows that the trade route was precisely what was at issue; and cedar timber shipped from the Levantine coast into Egypt reached a peak in the high period of the New Kingdom. Capture figures have to be discounted: Egyptian monuments count the enemy dead and taken, the horses and the metalware, and later scholars routinely cut those numbers by a factor of several, so they are better read as propaganda measures than as statistics. The hardest evidence of all is the Amarna correspondence: about three hundred and fifty letters survive, of which more than two hundred concern Mitanni.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是地理與商路：埃及要保住從西奈運出的銅礦、從黎巴嫩運入的雪松木，以及由巴比倫方向經米坦尼轉入的青金石，這條商路一旦被截斷，新王國的財政與神廟工程都要停滯；更關鍵的是幼發拉底河中游的卡爾凱美什與埃馬爾控制了從上游運銅、鉛、錫下行的通道，誰占住那兩城，誰就捏住幼發拉底河兩岸的關稅與人頭稅。中層是宗主權之爭：米坦尼大王在西屬的敘利亞諸邦面前自居宗主，埃及則要否認這層宗主關係，寧可自己收編卡脫納、圖尼普與阿勒頗。最內層是政治：圖特摩斯三世早年在宮中經歷繼承風波，成年後需要北方戰功來鞏固王位與一批有戰功的將領，敘利亞戰事既可收回邊境要塞，也能餵養軍功集團。前一次遠征雖把戰線推到幼發拉底河，卻沒有取得北岸的實際控制；大王隨即收緊對埃及商隊與北方城邦的約束，把兩國關係推向攤牌。於是法老再度自南敘利亞出發，目標不再是邊境小城，而是越過幼發拉底河，直取米坦尼本土的宗主中心。
causeEn: The war began for three layers of reason. The outermost was geography and trade: Egypt had to keep the copper coming down from Sinai, the cedar coming in from the Levant, and the lapis lazuli coming through Mitanni from Babylon, and if that route were cut the finances and the temple works of the New Kingdom would all stall. More decisively, Carchemish and Emar on the middle Euphrates controlled the passages down which copper, lead and tin moved from the upper reaches; whoever held those two cities held the tolls and the head-counts of both banks of the river. The middle layer was a struggle over overlordship: the Great King of Mitanni claimed the Syrian city-states as his own subordinates, while Egypt denied him that claim and preferred to take Qatna, Tunip and Aleppo into its own hand. The innermost layer was political: Thutmose III had been through a disputed succession in the palace as a youth, and once grown he needed northern victories to shore up his throne and to reward a circle of commanders; a Syrian war would recover the frontier fortresses and feed that circle. The previous expedition had driven the line of contact up to the Euphrates but had not gained effective control of the far bank, and the Great King promptly tightened his grip on Egyptian caravans and on the northern city-states, pushing the two courts towards a showdown. The pharaoh therefore set out from southern Syria once more, and this time the mark was not a string of small frontier towns but the country beyond the Euphrates and the very centre of the overlord's dominions.
impact: 對埃及，這場戰役把新王國的亞洲政策推到頂點。敘利亞自此更牢固地進入埃及的宗主體系：卡脫納、圖尼普、比布魯斯、西頓與阿勒頗按年進貢金、銀、鉛、錫、銅、象牙、馬匹、葡萄酒、食用油與人丁；埃及在本地設官徵收，敘利亞的葡萄酒與黎巴嫩雪松大量運入三角洲，神廟與船塢的建材因此不斷。對米坦尼，這是一場結構性挫敗：大王的西屬地盤被逐出幼發拉底河以西，王室退守上美索不達米亞，前1400年代起只能靠外交求生——向埃及借銀、乞求一尊自己的雕像、把自己的女兒送進埃及宮廷，甚至一度試圖與埃及王室結親。更遠地看，這條路也通向後來兩大強權在幼發拉底河上游的角力：前1400年代赫梯自安納托利亞南下，前13世紀埃及拉美西斯二世與赫梯王穆瓦塔里二世在卡爾凱美什會戰，讓這座城再次成為前線；而阿瑪納字母因記錄了米坦尼的求饒與兩國彼此試探，也成了後世重建青銅時代國際外交的第一手材料。
impactEn: For Egypt the war carried the Asian policy of the New Kingdom to its high point. Syria entered the Egyptian system of overlordship more firmly than before: Qatna, Tunip, Byblos, Sidon and Aleppo paid annual tribute in gold, silver, lead, tin, copper, ivory, horses, wine, oil and labour; Egypt stationed officials to collect it, and the wine of Syria and the cedar of the Levant poured into the Delta, feeding temple and dockyard building without end. For Mitanni this was a structural defeat: the Great King's western holdings were driven back from the far side of the Euphrates, the royal house withdrew to Upper Mesopotamia, and from the fifteenth century onward it could survive only by diplomacy — borrowing silver from Egypt, begging for a statue of itself, sending its own daughter into the Egyptian court, and at one point attempting a marriage alliance with the Egyptian royal house. Looking further ahead, the road ran on to the rivalry of the two great powers over the upper Euphrates: the Hittites came south out of Anatolia in the fifteenth century, and in the thirteenth century Ramses II of Egypt and the Hittite king Muwatalli II met at Carchemish, putting that city back on the frontier. And because the Amarna letters record Mitanni's supplication and the mutual testing of the two courts, they remain the primary document for reconstructing Bronze Age international diplomacy.
result: 結果是埃及以野戰勝利換來政治上限：敘利亞諸邦臣服於埃及宗主權之下，幼發拉底河成為埃及在北部的實際邊界，遠征的實際收穫不是佔土，而是名分與貢賦；大王一方雖未覆亡，仍保有「大王」名號與上美索不達米亞的核心地盤，往後數十年靠書信周旋，把國家拖到阿瑪納時代那種仰賴埃及援助的處境。若要說勝負怎樣算，埃及贏了戰役卻沒有贏下北界：它無法在幼發拉底河以北常駐軍隊，影響仍要靠一次次重兵出動維持。至於這場戰役在編年上的位置，維基百科的戰爭列表依現代學者肯尼斯·基欽的重建，把它放在前1440年代中葉圖特摩斯三世的一次北征，稱為第八次敘利亞戰役；也有學者把編號前後挪動，把這場越過幼發拉底河的戰役與其後連串的「巡遊敘利亞」併入同一計數。今天能確認的細節有限，戰役過程多靠卡爾納克年表的殘片、軍隊地名表、詩體銘文與後出的阿瑪納字母拼回；長矛手在前列頂住聯軍車兵的樣子、渡河之後的圍城，與「大王」遣使求和的記錄，是這場戰爭留給後世最清晰的畫面。
resultEn: The outcome was an Egyptian tactical victory exchanged for a political ceiling: the Syrian city-states became subjects of Egyptian overlordship and the Euphrates became Egypt's effective northern frontier, so what the expedition actually bought was recognition and tribute rather than territory. The Great King's state was not destroyed; it kept the title of Great King and the core of Upper Mesopotamia, and for decades turned to correspondence to hold the realm together, until it reached the position in the Amarna age of depending on Egyptian help. As for the arithmetic of the result: Egypt won the campaign but did not win the northern border, for it could not keep an army stationed beyond the Euphrates, and its influence had to be maintained by dispatching heavy columns again and again. As for where the war sits in the chronology, the list of wars on Wikipedia follows the reconstruction of the modern historian Kenneth Kitchen and places this northern expedition of Thutmose III in the middle of the fifteenth century, calling it the Eighth Syrian War; other scholars shift the numbering, merging this crossing of the Euphrates with the series of tours of Syria that came after. The details that can be confirmed today are few, and the course of the war has to be pieced together from the fragments of the Karnak annals, the army's topographical list, a poetic inscription and the later Amarna letters; the spearmen holding the front against the coalition chariots, the siege that followed the crossing, and the record of the Great King's envoys asking for terms are the clearest pictures the war has left behind.
